To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CpxR is a global regulator that represses curli gene expression in response to high osmolarity and that H-NS is a global regulator involved in curli gene expression.
CpxR is a negative regulator of csgD expression and that the Cpx system is activated in response to high-salt-content media.
CpxR and H-NS repress curli expression in response to high-salt- and sucrose-containing media, respectively, whereas OmpR activates the csgD expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of curli production by osmolarity, and the results indicate that the interplay between OmpR and H-NS and CpxR is involved.
a better understanding of the complex interplay between two-component pathways and global regulators in the regulation of curli genes.
understanding the complex regulatory network of the CpxR/Omp R interplay in the control of the csgD expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CpxA/CoxR two-component system, in response to high osmolarity, negatively regulates curli production by binding to multiple sites on the promoter of the csgD gene, which encodes a master regulator of curli gene expression.

CpxR is involved in the repression of csgD expression when the osmolarity of the medium is increased, while H-NS is involved in the regulation of csgD transcription when sucrose is present in the medium.
CpxR, OmpR, and H- NS act in concert to control the expression of csgD and, therefore, curli production in response to environmental osmolarity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CpxR is a repressor of csgD expression under conditions of high osmolarity, and that this repression is mediated through a complex interplay between OmpR and H-NS.
the CpxA/CxPR two-component system is a global regulator of the curli operon expression and is involved in the adaptation to osmotic stress.
the Cpx system acts as an osmolyte sensor and is able to repress csgD expression by binding directly to its promoter region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interplay between CpxR and OmpR is crucial for the regulation of the curlic expression in response to osmotic stress.

the CpxR protein, a global regulator involved in the response to environmental stresses and the maintenance of cell envelope homeostasis, is also a key player in the regulation of curli gene expression in response to osmolarity.
CpxR, a transcriptional activator of the Cpx regulon, acts also as a repressor of csgD expression by competing with the OmpR activator.
